slides.accentLine: A page nothing links to can be hard for Google to find.

slides.title: Find pages
slides.body: Google says it primarily finds pages through links from pages it already crawled.
slides.action: Open Search Console → Links → Top linked pages (internal). Find your key pages.
slides.example: A new product page that no category page or guide links to yet.

slides.title: Use real
slides.body: Google can generally only crawl a link that is an a element with an href attribute.
slides.action: Check menus, filters and buttons in the page source for an a tag with an href.
slides.example: A “View all” button that only works with a JavaScript click.

slides.title: Write clear
slides.body: Google wants anchor text that is descriptive, reasonably concise and relevant.
slides.action: Read only the anchor text. If it makes no sense on its own, rewrite it.
slides.example: “Click here” becomes “trail running shoes for wide feet”.

slides.title: Link in
slides.body: Google suggests linking to pages that help readers understand the page they are on.
slides.action: For each key page, find 2–3 related pages and add one link inside their text.
slides.example: A sizing guide links to the matching category page in its first paragraph.

slides.title: Don't chain
slides.body: Google advises against links right next to each other: readers can't tell them apart.
slides.action: Spread links through the copy, with words around each one.
slides.example: Not three links in a row, but one link per sentence.

slides.title: Five checks,
slides.seed: An AI can suggest link ideas from a list of your URLs.

slides.body: and I’ll send you a free SEO audit of your site.
